CHAPTER 6: HARMONIZING

THE MAJOR SCALE

he theory of chord construction and chord progressions is steeped in a process known as harmonizing the major scale-a system in which chords are constructed by stacking the notes of the major scale in 3rds. This harmonization process is also referred to as diatonic harmony.

DIATONIC TRIADS

Let's start by harmonizing the C major scale in triads. The first step is to write out the scale on the staff (. Fig. 1A the note that is a diatonic 3rd interval higher (two notes away in the same scale), above each scale step (. Fig. 1B now harmonized in 3rds. (Notice that some are major, while others are minor.) Finally, place the note that is a diatonic 3rd away on top of the second note (Fig. 1C). Now the process is complete: the C major scale harmonized in triads.
